summary: Ulrich Timme Kragh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Karmapa International Buddhist Institute and the University of Copenhagen, later holding posts at Geumgang University (2008–2010) and Copenhagen (~2011–2016).

Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Schulpforta, Bonn, and Berlin under teachers including Otto Jahn and Moriz Haupt. He held professorships at Greifswald (1876–1883), Göttingen (1883–1897), and Berlin (1897–1921).

Ulrike Roesler is a Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Münster. She taught at the universities of Freiburg and Marburg and was attested as Professor at the University of Oxford in 2019.

Uma Chakravarti is a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Delhi under doctoral supervisor D. Devahuti. She served as an educator at Miranda House from 1966 to 1998.

Umakant Premanand Shah was an Indologist and historian. He worked at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, where he was appointed deputy director in 1954 and head of the Ramayana Project in 1965, later serving as director at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1966–1975).

Umar Rolf von Ehrenfels was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Vienna (~1933–1937). He served as Head of Anthropology at the University of Madras (1949) and Guest-Professor at Heidelberg University (1961).
Umberto Norsa was an Indology scholar who studied law at the University of Bologna from ~1884 to 1888. He served as secretary at the Gabinetto di Lettura di Mantova from 1893 to 1938.
Umesh Kumar Singh is an Indologist who completed his BA at the University of Allahabad (1997–2000), his MA at Banaras Hindu University (2000–2002), and his PhD at the University of Delhi (2004–2010).

Umesha Mishra was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp. He worked at the University of Allahabad (~1923–1959) and served as director of the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies (~1951–1958).

Unapane Pemananda works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Peradeniya, South-Eastern Norway, Oslo, and the University of Hong Kong (PhD 2022–2025). In 2025, he joined the Faculty of Theology at the University of Oslo.

Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana works in Indology and related fields. He earned a BAMS from Bharathiar University, a master's from the University of Amsterdam, and a PhD from Yokohama National University, later holding posts at United Nations University (2010–2020) and TDU (2020).

Unrai Wogihara was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University, Strasbourg, and under Ernst Leumann and Junjirō Takakusu. He served as a professor at Shukyo University (~1907–1926) and Taisho University (~1926–1937).
Unsho Shaku was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Mount Koya in 1844. He taught Ekai Kawaguchi and founded Kairitsu Gakko, Juuzen Hokutsu, and the Juze-kai (1884).

Unuwaturabubule Mahinda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura. He taught at Sri Jayewardenepura (2015–2018) and served as Senior Lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka in 2026.

Uranchimeg B. Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London and held a post as a Research Associate at the University of Cambridge.

Uranchimeg Tsultem is a Buddhist studies and art history scholar who earned her PhD from UC Berkeley. She taught at the Mongolian National University of Arts and Culture (1995–2002) and was appointed Edgar and Dorothy Fehnel Chair at Herron/IUPUI in 2019.

Uranchimeg Tsultemin is a scholar in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, and held posts as Lecturer at UC Berkeley and Associate Professor at the National University of Mongolia.

Urs App is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who earned his PhD from Temple University. Mentored by Seizan Yanagida and Yoshitaka Iriya, he served as Associate Director at Hanazono University from 1989 to 1999.

Usha Nilsson was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. She was a faculty member at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where she taught Harvey B. Aronson and was attested as Emeritus Professor of Languages and Cultures of Asia.

Usha R. Jain is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of California, Berkeley. She taught Jinah Kim and served as Senior Lecturer Emerita at the University of California, Berkeley.
